solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Suit covers hotel put out for Penny (6)

indicatorNotes.put out for: one thing is put out to make way for another, so H leaves and P takes its place

blocks.note: shades = covers, as over lamps or eyes
H = hotel in the phonetic alphabet; this letter goes
p = penny; this letter comes in

annotation.surface: A man in a suit is sent out of a hotel for the sake of a woman called Penny.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Suit' reads as clothing but is the card suit. 'Penny' looks like a name and is just P.
annotation.definitionFit: A card-game sense: the pack has four suits, and this is the one marked with black spearheads.

indicatorNotes.fouled: fouled means messed up, so the letters are jumbled

annotation.surface: A tidy footballer is brought down, and the question is where it happened.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: a player fouled in that box on a football pitch wins a penalty kick.
annotation.definitionFit: The whole clue reads straight: the box in front of goal is exactly where a foul on an attacker matters most.

blocks.note: gen and dope are both slang for information

annotation.surface: A dig at Generation Y as a bunch of muddled youngsters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gen Y' reads as one phrase for a generation; split it, and Gen is information, which the slang also calls dope.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone dazed, slow and muddled.

blocks.note: a ring is a gang, as in a smuggling ring

annotation.surface: A prison gang is causing trouble inside.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface runs as one prison story, so 'creating trouble' seems to describe the gang; it is the definition, in the British sense of a stirrer who makes mischief.
annotation.definitionFit: A British idiom: to stir it is to set people against each other on purpose.

entries.clue: Duck initially spotted on eastern headland (6)

indicatorNotes.initially: at the start, so the first letter of 'spotted'
indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, S goes on after E

annotation.surface: A birdwatcher sees a duck on a headland to the east.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Duck' is the bird in the surface and the verb in the answer, as in ducking a question.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: both mean to avoid or get out of something.

entries.clue: Always eats when one has more of a piece of cake (6)

annotation.definition: more of a piece of cake

indicatorNotes.eats: what is eaten ends up inside, so EER takes AS and I into it

blocks.note: e'er, poetic for ever or always
as = when, as in 'as I left'

annotation.surface: Someone who always eats when another person has a second slice of cake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Piece of cake' looks like food and is the idiom for a simple task; 'more of' makes it the comparative.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'a piece of cake' is something simple, and 'more of' one asks for the comparative adjective.

entries.clue: A red latch bolted in large pen of flock? (9)

indicatorNotes.bolted: bolted means ran off wildly, so the letters scatter

annotation.surface: Sheep are shut in a big fold behind a gate with a red latch.
annotation.walkthrough: The flock is a church congregation, and a pen is where it gathers; the question mark flags that joke. 'Bolted' also plays on the latch.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful metaphor: a bishop's congregation is his flock, and the great church is where it is gathered in.

indicatorNotes.not: says the E must be left out

blocks.note: E = ecstasy, the drug; removed from PALE

annotation.surface: White porcelain from China, with no ecstasy in it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'China white' sounds like porcelain; China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate.
annotation.definitionFit: Rhyming slang: 'china plate' rhymes with mate, so china means a friend.

blocks.note: reads as the car she will need for six babies, and it is that too
a pregnant woman is herself carrying people, six of them

annotation.surface: A mother of six-to-be needs a bigger car.
annotation.walkthrough: A people carrier is the British name for a minivan. The joke: a woman expecting six babies is herself carrying people.
annotation.definitionFit: A British term for a minivan, a large car with seats for a big family.

indicatorNotes.shrouding: a shroud wraps round a body, so NIPS wraps round PINES

annotation.surface: Cold rain dripping on shrouded trees.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drops' looks like rain and is nips, small tots of whisky; 'Cold' is the noun.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: a nippy day is a chilly one, so the quality is coldness.

annotation.surface: It's time for everyone at the party to get high.
annotation.walkthrough: 'High' reads as drugged in the surface and means lofty in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean of great height, as a tower.

entries.clue: Slice of pastrami, chicken or ham (6)

indicatorNotes.Slice of: a slice is a small piece, so just the first letter

blocks.note: a layer is a hen kept for its eggs

annotation.surface: A deli order: pastrami, chicken or ham in the sandwich.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ham' sits with the meats but is a bad actor.
annotation.definitionFit: A theatre sense: a ham overacts, and an actor is also called by this older word.

indicatorNotes.Broadcasting: broadcasting is sending sound over the air, so we go by the sound

blocks.note: presence = company, as in 'I enjoy your presence'

annotation.surface: A TV company hands out prizes at a ceremony.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcasting company' reads as one noun, a TV channel; split it, and company is presence, said out loud.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to award a prize is to hand it over formally.

blocks.note: reads as a robbers' escape, but a getaway is also a short holiday
reads as the one at the wheel, but it is whoever makes the trip happen

annotation.surface: A heist's getaway driver.
annotation.walkthrough: The getaway car points to crime, but a getaway is also a short holiday, and the travel agent is the one who drives the booking.
annotation.definitionFit: The person who sells and arranges holidays is the force behind a getaway.

blocks.note: by = near, as in 'stand by me'

annotation.surface: A fortune-teller saying riches may be close.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' at the end looks like a hedge, but it is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as in 'do you by any chance know?', asking whether perhaps you do.

indicatorNotes.mistakenly: the letters are put in the wrong order

annotation.surface: A cross head teacher has made a blunder.
annotation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a blunder in the surface, but here it is something that blooms, a flower.
annotation.definitionFit: A crossword-only sense: a bloomer is anything that blooms, and this shrub is grown for its big flower heads.

indicatorNotes.pinching: to pinch is to steal, so DON is taken away

blocks.note: Ray Reardon, six-times world snooker champion
a don is a college fellow; removed from REARDON

annotation.surface: A snooker star pinches a man's backside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pinching' looks like a grope, but it means stealing. Ray Reardon was a Welsh player who won six world titles in the 1970s.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: both mean the backside.

entries.clue: Hard to fathom inner-city Tories somehow (8)

indicatorNotes.inner-: what is inner sits inside, so the jumbled TORIES goes inside EC
indicatorNotes.somehow: the letters of TORIES are arranged in some other way

blocks.note: EC = East Central, the postcode of the City of London

annotation.surface: Why inner-city voters are drawn to the Tories is a mystery.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Inner-city' reads as one word; split it, and inner puts the Tories inside the City, EC.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something known only to a few insiders is hard for others to fathom.

indicatorNotes.finally: takes the last letter of builder
indicatorNotes.installed: something installed is fitted inside, so the R is fitted into BED

blocks.note: a bed is a floor, as of a river or the sea

annotation.surface: A builder has finally put in a raised floor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Raised' looks like a floor that is lifted up, but it means brought up.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean brought up, as children or animals.

entries.clue: I forgive you after a bit of banter (8)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is a phrase the absolver says, not a noun; the clue asks what a person who says 'I forgive you' is

indicatorNotes.a bit of: just the first letter of banter
indicatorNotes.after: SOLVER comes after A and B

blocks.note: you, doing this crossword, are the solver

annotation.surface: After some teasing, a friend says all is forgiven.
annotation.walkthrough: 'You' is the reader of the puzzle, and a setter calls that person the solver. The whole thing reads as one sentence of forgiveness.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic twist: the one who says 'I forgive' is the person granting absolution.

entries.clue: Agree working dog follows nose in chase (6)

indicatorNotes.nose in: the nose is the front, so the first letter of chase
indicatorNotes.follows: to follow is to come behind, so the working dog comes after C

blocks.note: on = working, as of a machine

annotation.surface: A working dog, nose to the ground, happily joins the chase.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Working dog' reads as one idea, a sheepdog, but the two words are clued separately; 'nose in chase' is a dog's nose, turned into a first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, from Latin for running together: to be of the same opinion.

entries.clue: Part-Time Lover is a hit covered by Rush (8)

indicatorNotes.covered by: A RAM goes inside POUR, which covers it

blocks.note: pour = rush, as of a crowd or water

annotation.surface: Stevie Wonder's song Part-Time Lover was a hit, covered by the band Rush.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is about music: Part-Time Lover is a Stevie Wonder song and Rush a rock band. 'Covered' seems to mean a cover version.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: an illicit lover, often seen only now and then.

entries.clue: Piece of illustration framed by giant old master (6)

indicatorNotes.Piece of: just the first letter of illustration
indicatorNotes.framed by: TITAN goes round the I like a picture frame

annotation.surface: Part of an illustration framed by a giant of painting.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is all art, with 'framed' as the picture frame; it also puts the I inside the giant.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the great Venetian painter of the 1500s is one of the old masters.

entries.clue: Some student on ganja in a state (5)

indicatorNotes.Some: only some of the letters are used

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of student into the start of ganja

annotation.surface: A student high on cannabis is in a bad way.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In a state' reads as the idiom for being in a mess; split it, and a state is a nation.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Pacific island kingdom is one sovereign state.

entries.clue: Tedious record cut by Heart in earnest (4)

indicatorNotes.cut by: LOG is cut open by N going in
indicatorNotes.Heart in: the heart is the middle letter

blocks.note: a log is a record, as a ship's log

annotation.surface: A dull record cut by the band Heart.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is music again: Heart is a rock band. Here it is the middle letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as a long speech that drags on.

entries.clue: Not the first to block Yahoo! (3)

indicatorNotes.Not the first: tells you the first letter is not wanted, so it is dropped

blocks.note: block and loaf both mean the head; loaf's first letter goes

annotation.surface: A web user trying to block the site Yahoo! is not the first to do it.
annotation.walkthrough: Block and loaf are slang for head, as in 'use your loaf'. 'Yahoo!' looks like the web company, but a yahoo is a lout.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from Gulliver's Travels, where Yahoos are brutish humans: a coarse, stupid person.

blocks.note: permission to go ahead, as given by traffic lights
the gap between things, as under a bridge

annotation.surface: A green glow seen out in space.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In space' sounds like the cosmos, but space is just a gap.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: official permission to proceed, and the room left clear between two things.

entries.clue: Radio version of A Fine Romance (6)

indicatorNotes.Radio version of: on the radio we only hear it, so we go by the sound

annotation.surface: A radio play of the song A Fine Romance.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A Fine Romance' reads as the old song title; split it, and A Fine is 'a fair', while Romance is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a love relationship, often a secret one.

indicatorNotes.smuggled into: smuggled goods are slipped inside, so the H is slipped into CASTE

annotation.surface: Pure heroin smuggled into a railway station.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pure' looks like it describes the drug; it is the definition. Station is rank in life, not a railway stop.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: morally or sexually untainted.
